An independent adjudicator, shown the pack's questions without its source, could narrow this question using gam-cs-cp-001-q3. DOCTRINAL COUPLING succeeds in the stem-presupposition direction, and it is the one real coupling in this pack. q3's stem asks the reader to identify which cache 'met the smallest share of its requests without going to the slow store' — an ordinary comparative read across the table's rows, which the pack evidently treats as a legitimate and answerable question. That presupposition directly undercuts two of this item's four options. Option c claims the figures 'cannot be compared because the caches hold different numbers of records'; if that were the text's position, q3 would be asking the reader to perform a comparison the same source declares impossible. Option d claims a single day's hit rate is 'too short a period to be used at all'; that likewise would void the read q3 requires. Both are therefore improbable as the intended answer, narrowing this item from four options to a and b before any domain reasoning is applied. From there a falls to ordinary knowledge, leaving b. The narrowing is real but not decisive on its own, and it is redundant here because I reach b with high confidence from domain knowledge alone — so it inflates a solver's odds on this item without being the reason a competent solver gets it right. The remaining patterns fail: NUMERIC RECONSTRUCTION has no numbers to work with; SCALE DISCLOSURE is inapplicable, since q3's options are row labels with no magnitudes and cannot calibrate anything here; SHARED PARAMETER holds between this item and q3 (both read the same four-design table) but is inherent to a pack built on one source rather than a leak; CONVENTION AS CONSTANT fails, since no eviction policy figures in this item; ANSWER-AS-DISTRACTOR fails, since no sibling's correct answer appears among these options. q1 contributes nothing in either direction — I checked whether its 'a cache holds three records' could inform option c's claim about differing record counts and it cannot, as q1's cache is a separate hypothetical.
